workLogs.entry: Published Hue Light Control firmware on GitHub
workLogs.whatHappened: Created the public repository with ESP32 firmware, wiring illustrations, setup guide and an environment template. Connected the local origin remote and normalized Notion repository resource. Local credentials and generated files were excluded.

caseStudy.problem: Room lighting benefits from a control you can find by touch. I wanted one knob for brightness and on/off, with a screen that explains what is wrong when Wi-Fi or the bridge misbehaves, instead of a phone app.
caseStudy.role: Personal project. I wired the prototype, wrote the PlatformIO firmware, and documented setup, pin assignments, and diagnostics.
architecture: ESP32 reads a rotary encoder with push button (GPIO 19, 21, 22, internal pull-ups) and drives an SSD1306 OLED over I2C (GPIO 23/18).
A responsive input and display loop runs separately from a network task.
Lighting commands use local HTTPS to the Hue bridge with reused connections and paced brightness updates.
Bridge discovery tries mDNS first, then Philips' internet discovery service; settings persist across restarts.
decisions: Separate input/rendering from networking so the knob and screen stay responsive while requests are in flight.
Hold gestures show a countdown that always says what letting go will do (cancel, Settings, Restart), so one button can safely carry several actions.
Status is always visible: the header shows OK or a short tag such as WIFI, HUE, or AUTH, with the exact problem on the bottom line.
validation: On-device Test & fix checks configuration, Wi-Fi signal, bridge, Hue API key and room, and memory, reporting PASS/WARN/FAIL and repairing what it can.
Knob test (raw pin levels and a bad-step counter for noisy wiring), I2C bus scan, and screen test modes support hardware debugging.
Physical operation is builder-reported; there is no recorded video demonstration yet.
limitations: Controls one Hue room or zone and requires a Hue bridge and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.
Credentials are configured at build time; there is no web provisioning interface.
Bridge HTTPS uses the firmware's existing certificate behavior, not certificate pinning.
Project images are technical illustrations of the documented wiring, not photographs of the device.

chewsense.summary: An AirPods chewing-detection research pipeline with guided capture, Mac review and evaluation by independent recording sittings.
chewsense.description: ChewSense combines guided iPhone capture, local computer vision, human review on Mac and motion-model evaluation. The public Collect app records evidence; Live is an experimental detector. A November 10 validity study found that motion distinguishes chewing from pauses within held-out meals for one wearer, with evaluation grouped by sitting. A frozen detector also found both chewing bouts in one later recording. Talking, gum, drinking, soft food and other wearers remain open tests. An identified resampling issue may shift Live’s false-alarm rate; the study did not replace the bundled detector. Recordings can reach the Mac directly or through a temporary, phone-encrypted home-server mailbox.
chewsense.oneLiner: From synchronized AirPods capture to reviewed labels and measured chewing detection.

caseStudy.problem: Can AirPods motion distinguish chewing from other activity, and can paired video and review produce labels that make the evaluation credible?
caseStudy.role: I built the Swift capture and review apps, the local processing and transfer loop, and Python tools for motion-model training and evaluation.
architecture: Collect captures paired camera video and AirPods motion, with guided takes and editable coarse chewing spans.
A shared transfer client reaches the paired Mac directly; a temporary home-server mailbox holds phone-encrypted recordings when needed.
Local Vision produces candidates, Mac Review records human decisions, and Motion evaluates chewing-bout models. Predictions remain separate from verified labels.
Live replays the exported experimental feature model; Python and Swift parity checks test matching runtime behavior.
decisions: Keep recordings from one sitting together in development folds and resample sittings for uncertainty estimates.
Keep the locked test separate from exploration and score later development recordings once with the frozen detector.
Report threshold-selection sensitivity, recording-level decisions and split overlap alongside window scores.
Block export of sample-aligned training runs until Live implements the same resampling grid.
validation: November 10 study: 23 development recordings from one wearer, grouped into 12 sittings, five with chewing; within-meal AUC-ROC was 0.965 on held-out sittings.
The November 4 frozen detector found 50/50 labelled chewing windows and both bouts in one November 9 recording, with 0/88 false-positive windows. This is one recording, not population accuracy.
The encrypted mailbox handoff was exercised on a physical iPhone, including resumed upload, Mac collection and deletion after acknowledgment.
limitations: One wearer; no evidence yet for other people, other AirPods fits or free-living use.
Dedicated talking, gum, drinking and soft-food tests remain pending. The study included only 12 labelled talking windows.
Resampling can damp the vibration band and may shift Live’s false-alarm rate; this has not been measured as drift on the phone.
Individual chew counts, bites, swallows and health benefits are unvalidated. Collect’s public availability does not establish detector readiness.
The threshold-from-other-folds estimate reduces direct threshold selection on scored windows; it is not fully nested cross-validation.

chewsense.subtitle: Researching chewing detection with AirPods motion and paired video.

readme.content:
# ChewSense: capture, review and evaluate

ChewSense is a research workflow for learning from synchronized AirPods motion and eating video. The public Collect app captures evidence; the experimental detector is still being evaluated.

## How the pieces fit

1. **Collect — iPhone and iPad.** Record paired camera video and AirPods motion. Guided takes save instruction-derived coarse spans that the wearer can adjust; natural meals need manual marking.
2. **Vision and Review — Mac.** Local computer vision proposes events. Human review records accepted or corrected labels; predictions alone are never verified truth.
3. **Motion — Python.** Compare chewing-bout models, inspect errors and report uncertainty with recordings from one sitting kept together.
4. **Live — iPhone.** Replay an exported experimental detector and compare its output with Mac replay. This remains a research check.

Recording works without the Mac. Transfer uses the paired Mac directly when available, or a temporary home-server mailbox that receives phone-encrypted deposits for later Mac collection.

## What the November 10 study found

The development set contains 23 recordings from **one wearer**, grouped into **12 sittings**, five with chewing. The detector distinguished chewing from pauses within held-out meals (AUC-ROC 0.965). A detector frozen on November 4 also found both chewing bouts in one November 9 recording: 50 of 50 labelled chewing windows and no false positives among 88 labelled non-chewing windows.

Those are pilot results. Overlapping windows are not independent trials, and one later recording cannot establish general accuracy. The study kept the locked test out of fitting and scoring.

The strongest signal is jaw vibration in the 5–25 Hz band. A resampling issue can damp that band and may change the operating point in Live. Training now offers a sample-aligned comparison, with export blocked until Live supports the same grid. The study did not replace the bundled detector.

## What remains

Record dedicated Soft Food, Crunchy Food, Talking, Drinking and Gum Chewing takes, then a complete Natural Meal on another day. Score those development recordings with the frozen detector before retraining. Other wearers, free-living use, individual chew counts, bites, swallows and health outcomes remain unvalidated.

The [validity study](https://github.com/ZSturman/Chew-Sense/blob/main/docs/VALIDITY_2026-11-10.md) explains the evidence, threshold-selection limits and resampling issue. The [current repository](https://github.com/ZSturman/Chew-Sense) contains installation, architecture and development instructions.
